sanskrit_verse: शक्तो वा यदि दौरात्म्यान् न दद्याद् धनिने धनम् । राज्ञा दापयितव्यः स्याद् गृहीत्वांशं तु विंशकम् ॥
transliteration: śakto vā yadi daurātmyān na dadyād dhanine dhanam | rājñā dāpayitavyaḥ syād gṛhītvāṃśaṃ tu viṃśakam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: If a capable person, out of malice or neglect, refuses to give wealth rightfully due to another, the King shall ensure its delivery after taking a twentieth part thereof.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to enforce rightful claims
Causation is rooted in conscious refusal, not mere omission
Capacity-based responsibility demands action from those able to fulfill
Restoration logic requires return of what is rightfully owed
Consciousness alignment occurs through rectification, not punishment
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent.is_capable == TRUE AND agent.intentionally_withholds == TRUE) THEN (sovereign.enforce_transfer(asset, rightful_owner))
supreme_court_application: The Supreme Court must affirm that withholding assets by capable agents constitutes actionable violation. The sovereign's role is to restore balance, not punish intent. The deduction of one-twentieth ensures administrative sustainability without punitive overreach.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes the factual withholding; anupūrvaśaḥ traces the causal chain from capability to conscious refusal; proportional responsibility lies in returning the asset plus a nominal share; non-punitive reality rule upholds restoration as justice.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate asset verification process between parties
Deduct one-twentieth portion for state maintenance
Reintegrate defaulter via completion of societal service if needed
Ensure claimant receives full restitution without emotional burden
final_declaration: This law flows solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is restored when rightful possession is re-established. There is no punishment—only realignment of consciousness through corrective action. Reality itself adjudicates through divine sovereignty.
